model: General insurer free cash flow to equity capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; attributable cash earnings after regulatory capital retention, net debt zero)
model_label: Insurer FCFE at cost of equity, component-built on AASB 17 insurance revenue: net insurance financial result (underwriting result + net investment/discount income) - fees/overheads/D&A, taxed, less NCI, less capital retained to grow the regulatory capital base. Hybrid of the SKILL.md insurer row (BVPS compounding x exit P/B) and the operating-company engine, following the IAG.AX precedent (2026-09-23); BVPS x exit-P/B cross-check in inputs.notes.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026 AASB 17 insurance revenue (Consolidated statement of comprehensive income, FY26 AR line ~7419/583; equals the CSV 'Revenue' column). Suncorp discloses its margin (UITR) on this same base, unlike IAG which guides on net earned premium net of a large quota share -- Suncorp has no comparable large external quota share on the General Insurance book, so insurance revenue is the natural base and matches the company's own disclosure.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,058m ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY26 AR shareholder summary, excludes treasury shares), after the $400m/22.9m-share on-market buyback completed in FY26 and the Feb-2025 1-for-X share consolidation. Held FLAT in the engine (SBC ~$19-20m/yr is expensed inside fees/overheads); the FY27 $250m buyback (~13.5m shares at current price) is instead modelled as part of the capital-return flow via capex_pct_path (negative retention / net distribution), not as a share-count reduction, to keep per-share value comparisons on a constant-share basis the same way IAG.AX was built.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO. The flow discounted is attributable profit AFTER interest on Suncorp's $2,292m loan capital/subordinated notes (regulatory Tier 2 capital, not operating debt) and after net insurance finance expense (already inside the AASB 17 P&L). Deducting loan capital again would double-charge (SKILL.md: never subtract net debt from a post-interest flow). Cash of $997m sits inside shareholders'-funds and technical-reserve investment portfolios whose income is inside the flows, so it is not added either. total_debt and cash below are audit-only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 free cash flow to equity: NPAT attributable to owners 1,027 less capital retained ~64 (organic regulatory-capital growth funding, distinct from the FY27 $250m buyback which is a distribution of surplus-to-target capital already above the target range, not a claim on the ongoing flow). Pro-forma excess CET1 to mid-point of target range was $412m at 30 Jun 2026 (down from $997m at 30 Jun 2025) -- the FY26 buyback and special/final dividends drew that surplus down, which is why last_fcf is built from the smaller organic retention figure, not from the CET1 delta (M&A/one-off capital return, not organic).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: NPAT attributable to Suncorp Group Limited shareholders, FY2026 (cash earnings was $1,042m, NPAT + $15m after-tax acquisition-intangible amortisation add-back). Statutory operating cash flow ($1,585m FY26) is not usable for a component build: it swings with investment-portfolio trading and claims-reserve timing (FY23 OCF $742m vs FY24 $2,497m on an insurance revenue base moving only 13,697->18,354->13,697), and does not separate underwriting cash flow from portfolio churn.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payments $19-20m FY26/FY25 (FY26 AR note 9, line 7552) are expensed inside fees/overheads/other expenses, and the flow starts from profit AFTER that charge, so no second deduction is made and sbc is recorded as 0 in the flows. House and street bases coincide (band collapsed).
inputs.interest_income_note: Insurance investment income ($827m FY26 on insurance funds) and shareholders'-funds/interest revenue are LEFT IN the flows inside the net insurance financial result and the segment interest-revenue lines, because the matching investment assets are not added to equity value separately and no net debt is deducted (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the AUD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: the flow is post-interest and no debt is deducted. AUD 10-year government yield ~4.3% (Sept 2026) + 5.5% equity risk premium x beta 0.80 (large-cap domestic-and-NZ general insurer; demand is largely compulsory/mortgage-linked and non-discretionary, giving a lower earnings beta than IAG's 0.85 used for a similar-sized peer, offset slightly by Suncorp's smaller diversification post-bank-sale) = 8.7%, rounded to 9.0% to match the IAG.AX peer rate and keep both insurers comparable on the same AUD cost-of-equity basis. Catastrophe/reserve volatility is charged in the bear scenario's flows and its scenario weight, not stacked on the rate (charge risk once). One rate across all scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost: lease liabilities are small ($367-415m, FY26 AR note, mostly office premises) and lease principal/interest sit inside fees/overheads/D&A, therefore inside the margin path; not modelled as debt (the model carries none).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged IN THE FLOWS, folded directly into ebitda_margin_path (the engine has no separate NCI driver): non-controlling interests (managed-funds units consolidated under AASB 10, not an operating joint-venture minority like IAG's RACV/RACQ) took $40m of FY26 post-tax profit (3.7% of $1,067m consolidated PAT; FY25 $50m, 2.7-3.1%; smaller and steadier than IAG's ~2.4%-of-NEP NCI leakage). The pretax-equivalent deduction that reproduces the reported $1,027m attributable NPAT exactly from the $1,513m PBT and 29.5% tax rate is 0.37% of insurance revenue (40 / (1-0.295) / 15,247 = 0.37%); every ebitda_margin_path value below has this 0.37pp already subtracted, so the engine's pretax margin x (1-tax) reproduces attributable-to-owners NPAT directly. FY26 check: (9.92 - 0.37)% x 15,247 x (1-0.295) = 1,026.8 vs reported 1,027 (ties).
inputs.tax_note: ~29.5% effective Australian/NZ blended corporate rate applied to attributable pre-tax profit: FY26 effective 446/1,513 = 29.5%, FY25 644/2,254 = 28.6%, FY24 429/1,400 = 30.6%. No shelter, no ramp; held at 29.5% (the FY26 actual, close to the 3-year average) across all years and scenarios.
inputs.engine_mapping: revenue = AASB 17 insurance revenue. ebitda_margin_path = attributable pre-tax profit / insurance revenue = net insurance financial result % (underwriting result + net investment/discount income, on revenue) - fees/overheads/D&A net %. FY26 actual: 11.60 (NIFR%) - 1.68 (fees+overheads+D&A net%) = 9.92% pretax margin; net of the 0.37%-of-revenue NCI fold-in (9.92-0.37=9.55%) x (1-0.295) x 15,247 = 1,026.8 vs reported attributable NPAT 1,027 (ties). FY25 comparable (continuing): NIFR% 16.25 - fees/other% 1.19 = 15.06% PBT margin (peak year: exceptional prior-year reserve releases + high investment income ahead of the FY26 bond mark-to-market losses). FY24: NIFR% 12.46 - fees/other% 2.31 = 10.15% (check: 1400/13697=10.22%, close). FY23: NIFR% 10.56%, PBT% 8.28%. da_pct_path = 0 (D&A is inside the fees/overheads/D&A net% already netted into the margin path, not added back separately, because there is no separate owner-FCF capex layer here). capex_pct_path = equity retained to grow the regulatory capital base as insurance revenue grows: General Insurance total-capital PCA coverage was 1.71x at FY26 (1.80x FY25, 1.58x FY24) against an implied target band of roughly 1.6-1.8x (mid ~1.7x); CET1 pro-forma excess to target midpoint fell from $997m (FY25) to $412m (FY26) as FY26's $400m buyback plus dividends drew down surplus faster than organic capital generation. With CET1 already above target and active de-capitalisation underway (ongoing FY27 buyback), organic retention is modelled thin: ~0.42 x revenue growth (roughly Suncorp's capital intensity, i.e. every $1 of insurance-revenue growth requires ~$0.42 of retained capital to hold the PCA multiple, lower than IAG's 0.35x-of-NEP-growth-at-28%-PCA-intensity scaled up because Suncorp's PCA/revenue ratio is higher post-bank-sale with a smaller, more capital-intensive pure-insurance base). FY27 capex_pct ~0.42% of revenue (~$66m, ~6% of attributable NPAT), fading toward ~0.3% at 2.5% terminal growth. FCF out of the engine is therefore FCFE = attributable NPAT - organic growth capital (excludes the one-off/surplus-driven $250m FY27 buyback and special dividends, which are a distribution of capital already above target, not part of the recurring flow the DCF discounts -- consistent with treating that surplus in the equity bridge instead of inflating the discounted flow).
inputs.notes: MODEL: dcf-methods SKILL.md routes an insurer to 'BVPS compounding x exit P/B'. Suncorp does not compound book: shareholders' equity fell from $13,844m (FY24) to $10,362m (FY26) purely because of the ~$3.8bn FY25 capital return following the Suncorp Bank sale to ANZ (completed 31 Jul 2024), and the payout ratio target is 60-80% of cash earnings plus ongoing buybacks -- book value is a residual of capital management, not a growth compounding engine. Following the IAG.AX precedent (researched 2026-09-23, same SKILL.md override rationale), the model instead discounts free cash flow to equity at the cost of equity with net debt at zero, built on the engine so the dashboard reproduces it. STRUCTURAL BREAK: the Suncorp Bank divestment (completed 31 Jul 2024, deconsolidated from FY2025) shrank total assets from ~$111.7bn (FY2024) to ~$30.2bn (FY2025) and cut FY2025 shares outstanding via the Feb-2025 share consolidation associated with the $3.00/share capital return; no continuity assumption is drawn across this break -- FY2024 and earlier are used only for the insurance-margin percentage series (NIFR%, fees/other%), which are unaffected by the bank's presence, never for revenue, share-count or balance-sheet CAGRs. FY2019 also carries a -$881m discontinued-operations loss on the Wealth business sale, excluded as non-recurring and not used in any growth or margin calculation. BVPS x EXIT P/B CROSS-CHECK (memo): net tangible assets per share $5.21 (FY26) / $5.33 (FY25); Cash RoTE well above Suncorp's targeted through-the-cycle cost of equity (management's own strategic target); sustainable P/B = (ROE-g)/(CoE-g). Using a normalised ~18% cash RoTE on tangible equity, 9% CoE, 2.5% terminal g: (0.18-0.025)/(0.09-0.025)=2.38x -> ~$12.4 on FY26 NTA/share of $5.21 -- but Suncorp's book is intentionally kept thin relative to earnings power (surplus capital is continuously returned, not retained), so a P/B-on-thin-NTA cross-check understates value versus a P/B-on-normalised-capital-intensity view; the FCFE-at-CoE base case below is the primary answer, consistent with the IAG.AX build. ANCHORS: FY26 (30 Jun 2026) NPAT (owners) 1,027, cash earnings 1,042, insurance revenue 15,247, GWP 15,407 (+2.7%), UITR 11.8% (top of 10-12% target range; FY25 UITR 11.9%), natural hazard costs $2,024m vs $1,770m allowance (+$254m overrun), net investment income $553m (down from $766m FY25 on bond MTM losses), CET1 pro-forma excess to target midpoint $412m, GI total-capital PCA coverage 1.71x, DPS 69c ordinary + 10c special (70.5% payout of cash earnings), NTA/share $5.21. FY27 guidance: GWP growth 3-5%, UITR expected top half of 10-12% range, expense ratio broadly in line with FY26, prior-year reserve releases ~0.4% of net insurance revenue, payout ratio around mid-point of 60-80% of cash earnings, up to $250m further on-market buyback targeted to complete by end FY27. New 5-year multi-year aggregate reinsurance cover from 30 Jun 2026 (up to $800m/yr, $2.4bn over 5 years) caps FY27 natural hazard downside to ~$50m in 90% of scenarios, materially de-risking the bear tail versus the historical natural-hazard-overrun pattern (overrun in most of the last 5 years). Metrics.csv 'Revenue' equals AASB 17 insurance revenue; 'FreeCashFlow' and 'CapEx' are blank by design (not meaningful for an insurer).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T06:10:08Z (Yahoo Finance chart API, regular session). 52-week range 13.80-20.85.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (FY26 AR shareholder summary; excludes treasury shares)

equity_bridge.item: Pro-forma excess CET1 above mid-point of target operating range (net of FY26 dividends)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR Group capital position table, line 9184; earmarked for the announced FY27 $250m buyback and beyond -- surplus capital above the recurring organic-retention flow the DCF discounts

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 GWP guidance midpoint (3-5%) less a small NEP/insurance-revenue lag; near-term insurance-revenue path, not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is deeply negative (-8.6% 3yr, -5.0% 5yr) purely from the ~$3.8bn FY25 capital return funded by the Suncorp Bank sale proceeds, and revenue/EPS CAGRs straddle the FY2024->FY2025 deconsolidation of the Bank (Revenue column is total-company including the Bank pre-FY2025, insurance-only from FY2025) -- none of these headline CAGRs are usable growth signals for a pure-play insurer projection. Insurance-revenue-only CAGR (FY23 12,081 -> FY26 15,247, +8.0% 3yr) is the clean series and is faded toward the FY27 GWP guidance midpoint (4%) then down to a 2.5% terminal rate, consistent with the IAG.AX peer build.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGR (1.9%) is distorted by the FY25 special one-off items (bank-sale gain, reserve-release peak) and the FY25 share consolidation; not used as a growth anchor. Reported insurance/underwriting margins (PBT % of insurance revenue) over the last four years: FY23 8.3%, FY24 10.2% (10.15% check), FY25 15.1% (peak, exceptional reserve releases + high investment income before FY26 bond MTM losses), FY26 9.9% -- mean of the four years ~10.9%, close to the FY24/FY26 non-peak level, which anchors the long-run base margin below the FY25 peak.

base.growth_rationale: Insurance revenue growth. FY27 4.0%: GWP guidance 3-5% (midpoint 4%) reflects continued pricing for inflation in Consumer and Personal Injury, partly offset by ongoing softness in the commercial market and NZ (GWP -4.8% FY26 in that segment); insurance revenue tracks GWP with a modest lag as premium earns through. Then fades from rate-driven mid-single-digit (claims-inflation pass-through, modest volume growth) to 2.5% terminal by FY35, in line with the IAG.AX peer's terminal assumption.
base.margin_rationale: Attributable pre-tax margin on insurance revenue = net insurance financial result % (underwriting margin + net investment/discount income) - fees/overheads/D&A net %. FY27 base ~10.0%: UITR guided top-half of 10-12% (call it 11.3%) less a normalised natural-hazard drag now the new 5-year aggregate reinsurance cover caps FY27 downside to ~$50m in 90% of scenarios (so FY27 reported margin should sit closer to underlying than FY26's hazard-overrun year), plus a modest normalisation of investment income (higher running yield of 5.1% on the AU portfolio, offset by ongoing bond-market mark-to-market noise) less fees/overheads/D&A drag of ~1.6-1.8% -- broadly the FY24/FY26 non-peak margin level of ~10%. Fades slightly to 9.1% by the terminal year as natural-hazard allowances continue rising with climate trend (allowance +1.7% FY26->FY27 to $1,800m) and the softer NZ/commercial cycle persists, partially offset by Digital Insurer cost-out. Excludes the FY25 peak (15.1%, driven by exceptional prior-year reserve releases and a temporarily high investment yield ahead of FY26's bond MTM losses) as non-recurring. Path shown is NET of the ~0.37%-of-revenue NCI deduction (see inputs.nci_treatment); pre-NCI it would be ~0.37pp higher throughout.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold the General Insurance total-capital PCA coverage near its ~1.6-1.8x target band as insurance revenue grows: ~0.42 x revenue growth in FY27, moderating toward ~0.3x at the 2.5% terminal growth rate as the capital base matures and normal per-year organic retention (rather than the FY26 CET1 drawdown from de-capitalisation) becomes the steady state. This organic-retention capex excludes the FY27 $250m buyback of surplus-to-target capital, which is a one-off distribution captured in the equity bridge, not a recurring claim on the discounted flow.

bull.growth_rationale: FY27 at the top of guidance (GWP +5%): Consumer and Personal Injury pricing initiatives continue to earn through strongly, AA Insurance (NZ) direct growth offsets the softer NZ commercial cycle, and the Digital Insurer platform (Duck Creek rollout) supports better retention and cross-sell. Growth stays mid-single-digit for longer as the reinsurance-cost de-risking (multi-year aggregate cover) supports more aggressive volume growth without proportionate capital strain.
bull.margin_rationale: UITR sustained at the top of the 10-12% range (11.8-11.9%, the FY26/FY25 underlying levels) with natural hazard experience running inside the new aggregate-cover-protected allowance every year (no repeat of the FY26 $254m overrun), Digital Insurer cost-out lowering the expense ratio further, and investment yields holding up as bond markets stabilise. Long-run 10.3% versus the base's 9.1%, reflecting a structurally better hazard/reinsurance outcome, not a one-off reserve-release peak like FY25. Path shown is NET of the ~0.37%-of-revenue NCI deduction (see inputs.nci_treatment).
bull.capex_rationale: Slightly higher retention to fund the faster growth path while maintaining the PCA coverage band; still modest given Suncorp's ongoing capital-return posture.

bear.growth_rationale: FY27 misses the bottom of guidance (GWP +2-3%): NZ GWP keeps contracting on a soft commercial cycle and weak economy, affordability-driven lapses and political pressure cap AU rate increases even as claims inflation continues, and the commercial market stays 'fiercely competitive'. Growth settles at 1.5-2%, below claims inflation, consistent with a structurally more competitive market (IAG post-RACQ is larger and more aggressive).
bear.margin_rationale: A natural hazard year that breaches even the new aggregate reinsurance cover's 90th-percentile protection (a >1-in-10 outcome) in FY27 and again a large event in FY28, reinsurance repricing on renewal, continued net investment income softness from further bond market volatility, and no prior-year reserve releases (Personal Injury/CTP releases assumed exhausted). UITR falls toward the bottom of or below the 10-12% target range. Long-run margin ~7.5%, below the FY23 trough level (8.3%), reflecting a structurally higher natural-hazard/reinsurance cost environment (climate trend) that the base case's cover partially offsets but does not eliminate. Path shown is NET of the ~0.37%-of-revenue NCI deduction (see inputs.nci_treatment).
bear.capex_rationale: Higher capital intensity: rising natural-hazard allowances lift the PCA base, and the buyback programme stops (surplus capital consumed defending the target range), so a larger share of a smaller profit is retained.

scenario_narratives.base: Suncorp delivers FY27 inside guidance (insurance revenue +4%, UITR top-half of the 10-12% range, expense ratio broadly flat), and the new 5-year aggregate reinsurance cover normalises the reported margin closer to underlying by capping natural-hazard downside to ~$50m in 90% of scenarios -- a material de-risking versus FY26's $254m overrun. Attributable pre-tax margin on insurance revenue settles around 10% (the FY24/FY26 non-peak level, well below FY25's exceptional 15.1% reserve-release peak) and fades slowly toward 9.1% as climate-driven natural-hazard allowances keep rising and the NZ commercial cycle stays soft, only partly offset by Digital Insurer cost-out. Around 90%+ of profit is distributed (60-80% ordinary dividend payout of cash earnings plus ongoing buybacks funded from capital already above the target range); the rest funds the thin organic capital retention a growing premium base requires. The axes that matter are natural-hazard experience versus the (now partially reinsured) allowance, the UITR trend, and net investment income on ~$5-6bn of insurance and shareholders' funds.
scenario_narratives.bull: FY27 comes in at the top of guidance (insurance revenue +5%) with UITR sustained at 11.8-11.9% every year as the new aggregate reinsurance cover keeps natural hazard experience inside allowance, Digital Insurer/Duck Creek delivers the promised cost-to-serve reduction, and AA Insurance NZ growth offsets a stabilising (not deteriorating) NZ commercial market. Margin holds near 10.3-11.3% long run rather than fading, since the reinsurance de-risking is structural, not cyclical. Growth compounds mid-single-digit for longer before settling at a 3% terminal rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: Suncorp posts back-to-back natural hazard years that breach even the new aggregate cover's 90th-percentile protection, reinsurance costs reprice higher on renewal, NZ GWP keeps contracting on a soft economy and competitive intermediated market, and affordability politics cap AU rate increases even as claims inflation persists. UITR falls toward or below the bottom of the 10-12% target range and stays there; no further meaningful reserve releases. Growth settles at 1.5-2%, below claims inflation, and the buyback programme pauses as capital is consumed defending the PCA target. No solvency question (CET1 comfortably above target even in a stress year, multi-year aggregate reinsurance in place), so this is an earnings-and-multiple case, not a survival case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 adjusted to 25/50/25, matching the IAG.AX peer build: natural-catastrophe volatility is rated high in the Analysis JSON, FY26 missed its natural-hazard allowance by $254m (continuing a multi-year pattern of overruns), and climate trend is structurally raising the allowance every year ($1,770m FY26 -> $1,800m FY27). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it requires the new aggregate reinsurance cover to hold perfectly for a decade with zero breach of the 90th-percentile protection and Digital Insurer cost-out to land on schedule -- both plausible but not the base case. Base 50%, anchored on Suncorp's own FY27 guidance and the new reinsurance structure genuinely reducing (not eliminating) tail risk versus the pre-2026 program.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Suncorp is valued on the cash it can actually pay its shareholders as a pure-play Trans-Tasman general insurer: attributable profit on AASB 17 insurance revenue, after interest on regulatory capital instruments and after the small managed-funds-units minority interest, less the thin equity it must retain to hold its capital coverage ratio as premium grows, discounted at a 9% AUD cost of equity with no separate debt deduction (matching the IAG.AX peer methodology and rate). The base case, with the underwriting-plus-investment margin normalising to the FY24/FY26 level of ~10% (well below the FY25 peak of 15.1%, which relied on exceptional reserve releases and pre-MTM-loss investment income) and growth fading from the FY27 guidance midpoint to 2.5% terminal, is the primary answer. Suncorp does not compound book value -- the ~$3.8bn FY25 capital return from the Bank sale proceeds and the ongoing 60-80%-of-cash-earnings payout plus buybacks mean shareholders' equity is a residual of capital management, not a growth engine -- so the SKILL.md default of BVPS-compounding x exit-P/B was overridden in favour of the same FCFE-at-cost-of-equity engine used for IAG.AX, for the same reason.
key_risks_to_valuation: Natural hazard experience versus allowance is the single largest swing: the FY26 $254m overrun (on an $1,770m allowance) shows the allowance itself is not a reliable cap; the new 5-year aggregate reinsurance cover reduces but does not eliminate this risk (protects only to a 90th-percentile confidence, and only from 30 Jun 2026).

The UITR guided at the top half of 10-12% for FY27 is management's own underlying (ex-hazard-experience, ex-reserve-movement) measure; the reported margin the DCF actually discounts can differ materially in either direction depending on hazard experience and reserve releases in any given year.

Net investment income (FY26 $553m, down from $766m FY25) is sensitive to both the running yield on the ~$5-6bn insurance/shareholders'-funds portfolio and mark-to-market movements as rates change; a further rate rise would help running yield but hurt near-term MTM, and vice versa.

Capital retention is modelled at ~0.3-0.5x revenue growth to hold the PCA coverage ratio near its historical 1.6-1.8x band; an APRA capital-standard change or the reinsurance cover proving less effective than modelled would raise the intensity and cut FCFE.
Discount rate: the base case is terminal-heavy (Gordon growth at 9%/2.5% binds near the 15x cap); each 1pp move in the cost of equity moves the value materially.

NZ segment (Suncorp New Zealand) GWP contracted 4.8% in FY26 on a soft commercial cycle and weak economy; a sustained NZ downturn would be a persistent drag not fully captured if the base case's fade assumes stabilisation.
IAG (larger post-RACQ) and QBE compete aggressively on price; a hardening competitive response to Suncorp's premium increases could cap future GWP growth below the 3-5% FY27 guidance range.
